full_judgment:
Is the suit is barred for mis-joinder and non-joinder of the parties? 

 15. In his examination in cross the PW 1 denied that the destination port was not known to the master of the defendant No. 1 vessel up to 1-2-2009 when the vessel was called at South Africa for taking bunkers. No prove was given by the defendants as to non-availability of bunker at Cape Town and Port Durban. The bad weather and adverse current cannot call such a long delay. The estimated voyage was 30 days from Port of Santos to Chittagong Port. By different e-mails the plaintiff has informed its loss. 

 32. The learned Advocate Mr Md Ruhul Amin next argued that the bank interest on the L/C value had to be paid by the plaintiff company for the delay period of delivering the cargo to the plaintiff. But due to non-delivery of the cargo, the plaintiff had to incur the expenses in respect of the interest on this delayed period. These factual aspects have been proved by adequate documents as have been procured from the bank and submitted as exhibit. 

 35. The learned Advocate Mr Md Ruhul Amin finally argued that the loss to the plaintiff has been caused because of the non-delivery of raw material on actual point of time and because the delay was for 30 days the plaintiff has to incur all the expenses and losses due to the negligent voyage of the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV Clio' and, as such, the entire loss is attributable to the shoulder of the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV Clio'. Therefore, the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV Clio' is liable to compensate the loss of plaintiff by way of damage.
